summary: Configured chrony on node1 (AlmaLinux 9) as the internal NTP server for the cluster — added `allow 10.100.35.0/24` and `local stratum 10` to /etc/chrony.conf, opened the firewalld ntp service — while node1 continues syncing from the public pool for accuracy. Configured node2 to point exclusively at node1 (`server 10.100.35.10 iburst`, removed the public pool line). Verified node2 syncs against node1 (chronyc sources shows node1 as `^*` current best source, Reference ID 10.100.35.10) and node1 shows node2 as an active NTP client. Then ran the mandatory sequential restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot IDs and healthy chrony state, restarted node1 first and confirmed boot-ID change plus config/firewall persistence and successful public-pool resync, then restarted node2 and confirmed boot-ID change plus persisted client config and successful resync against node1.
actions_performed: Inspected OS and chrony presence on node1/node2 (AlmaLinux 9.6, chronyd active on both)
Captured baseline chrony tracking/sources on both nodes (both synced to public pool.ntp.org, stratum 5)
Edited node1 /etc/chrony.conf: added 'allow 10.100.35.0/24' and enabled 'local stratum 10', backed up original to chrony.conf.bak
Restarted chronyd on node1 and opened firewalld ntp service (permanent + reload)
Edited node2 /etc/chrony.conf: replaced 'pool 2.almalinux.pool.ntp.org iburst' with 'server 10.100.35.10 iburst', backed up original
Restarted chronyd on node2 and verified single source is node1 via chronyc -n sources -v
Verified node1 chronyc clients shows node2 actively polling it via NTP

Captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony health on node1, issued systemctl reboot (backgrounded), polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed, verified chronyd active, config/firewall persisted, and node1 resynced to public pool

Captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony health on node2, issued systemctl reboot (backgrounded), polled until exec succeeded again, confirmed boot_id changed, verified chronyd active, config persisted, and node2 resynced to node1 as sole source

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal time source (server role) for the cluster
evidence.summary: node1's chrony.conf updated with allow 10.100.35.0/24 and local stratum 10, chronyd restarted, firewalld ntp service opened, and chronyc clients shows node2 actively polling node1 over NTP.

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of a public time server
evidence.summary: node2's chrony.conf pool line replaced with 'server 10.100.35.10 iburst'; chronyc -n sources -v confirms 10.100.35.10 (node1) is the sole and current-best (^*) source, and no DHCP-provided NTP sources exist.
Captured node1 boot_id (5fb1b173-c1c8-4647-b118-0145511f0fcc) and healthy chronyc tracking output before restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec failed with connection reset (node down); polling succeeded with new boot_id 12627f89-03ae-4828-b0d1-85e32823614b (changed from baseline); post-restart chronyd active, config/firewall persisted, and node resynced to public NTP (stratum 5).

evidence.requirement: Cluster time-sync relationship intact after node1 restart (node2 unaffected/recovered)
evidence.summary: After node1 came back, node2's chronyc sources still shows 10.100.35.10 as current-best (^*) source, confirming the sync relationship survived node1's restart.
Captured node2 boot_id (d6298ced-a924-4ce7-bbed-0fb8179eda8e) and confirmed chronyd active before restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec failed with connection reset (node down); polling succeeded with new boot_id 3fcad5e7-a358-4a30-bf5d-422e316fd54d (changed from baseline); post-restart chronyd active, server config persisted, and node2 resynced with node1 (10.100.35.10) as sole current-best source.
